chapterFiles.title: Adapa and the South Wind — the lost-immortality myth; the Ea-deception crux

titles.es: Adapa y el Viento del Sur
titles.fr: Adapa et le Vent du Sud

versionTitles.ja: ホイール・オブ・ヘブン訳

versionSource: Best-effort reconstruction from named scholarly editions (Knudtzon 1915 PD for Frag A; Picchioni 1981; Izre'el 2001 LSU 10; Foster 2005 Before the Muses 3rd ed)
sourceCitation: Izre'el, S., Adapa and the South Wind: Language Has the Power of Life and Death (Mesopotamian Civilizations 10, Winona Lake 2001) — the modern critical edition; Foster, B. R., Before the Muses, 3rd ed. (Bethesda 2005), pp. 525-530; Picchioni 1981; Knudtzon 1915 (PD) for Fragment A.

subtitles.en: The Akkadian wisdom-and-lost-immortality myth — Adapa breaks the wing of the South Wind by speech-act; Anu summons him to heaven; Ea instructs him to refuse the food and water Anu will offer; Adapa refuses what was actually food/water of life; humanity loses immortality

descriptions.en: The Akkadian myth of Adapa, who refuses the food of life offered by Anu, translated from four tablet fragments and read beside Genesis 3:22, with line notes.
descriptions.verificationNote: This translation is produced from a best-effort reconstruction of the Akkadian transliteration. The sense of each line is well-attested across multiple scholarly editions and should match downstream English faithfully. Verification of the precise sign-by-sign Akkadian transliteration against Izre'el 2001 LSU 10 is pending; corrections welcome.
